absent: Numeric values and bit positions of packed descriptor flags, event flags and wrap selector are not shown.
Implementation and ordering guarantees of the paired use guard and barrier helpers are not shown.
Head allocation, descriptor chaining and mapping policy for ordered insertion beyond the failure rollback tail are not shown.
Ring geometry negotiation, alignment handling and shrink rules for creation and resize are not shown.
RTC message layout, timeout duration, completion callback and clock identifier allocation are not shown.
Behaviour of split ring counterparts referenced by operation tables is not shown.
Meaning of weak barriers, context flag and event triggered state is not shown.

findings.text: Queue creation chooses between packed and split construction according to whether the device negotiated the packed ring feature, forwarding index, size, alignment, barrier mode, shrink permission, context, notification and callback attributes plus mapping information to the chosen constructor.

A queue can be instantiated over caller supplied memory, interpreting that memory as a packed descriptor area or as a split area depending on the same negotiated feature, with the device parent used for mapping context.
A device wide clear operation visits every queue belonging to the device and marks each as no longer broken, allowing subsequent obtain operations to proceed.
The split layout accessor returns a reference to the stored split ring of the given queue, offering read only visibility of its current geometry.

Mapping synchronization helpers are inert when the queue does not use the mapping interface, otherwise they delegate the need check and the processor or device synchronization for a range to either a device supplied mapping operation set or the generic direct mapping layer.

Time services expose a hardware timestamp selector that reports a fixed virtual counter kind and architecture counter identity, a class lookup from a generic device, and a blocking clock read that transfers a read request for a clock identifier and returns a nanosecond reading.
The RTC class record associates a controller pointer with a kernel RTC handle, a numeric virtual clock identifier, and a stopped marker that blocks further use while set.

Four operation tables share most handlers but diverge systematically between split and packed variants for adding, obtaining, polling, detachment, reclamation and reset, with separate in order flavours that differ only in obtain and availability testing, plus a forward declaration of the packed table.
Device event state is observed as one thirty two bit snapshot combining an offset plus wrap selector with a mode flag, allowing a consistent view of the host suppression request.

Packed queue entry, completion, reclamation and event control paths bracket their work with a paired use guard that must be entered on arrival and released on every exit including early no work and broken paths.
Clearing broken state holds the device queue list guard across the entire traversal, preventing concurrent membership change while each queue flag is updated with ordered store semantics.

Request transfer holds the per queue interrupt saving spin guard only across descriptor enqueue plus kick decision, releasing before notification and blocking wait, so completion handling does not deadlock.
A packed descriptor counts as device completed only when its availability and used signals agree with each other and with the expected wrap polarity for the current lap.
Queues flagged broken never hand out a buffer; obtain paths test that flag first and report absence without touching ring state.

Completion handling validates that the reclaimed identifier lies within ring bounds and corresponds to a live head with stored driver data, treating out of range or non head values as ring corruption.

Reclamation returns the descriptor count of the finished chain to the free pool, and for unordered use also splices the chain back onto the free list, while ordered use relies on positional advance alone.

The consumed position advances by the chain length, wrapping modulo ring size with polarity inversion, published with single store semantics and, when selective host wake is active, mirrored to the driver event offset with ordering.
Kick requirement is a pure function of host suppression mode and the interval of newly published avail entries, evaluated after prior publishes are made visible and with pending count cleared.

Enabling callbacks publishes event offset before mode with a barrier, records the requested mode in a shadow copy, and delayed enabling arms a future offset partway through outstanding buffers rather than the current consumed point.

Indirect descriptor tables are unmapped for every entry when mapping is active, freed exactly once, and the stored table pointer cleared; without indirection the stored context pointer is handed back when the caller asks for it.
Avail and used wrap polarities each invert on every lap around the ring, so the same index denotes alternating generations and stale completions from the prior lap are distinguishable.

Callback suppression shadow moves between disabled and enabled or selective states; disabling writes the device only when the shadow actually changes and no trigger is already pending, enabling writes only when leaving disabled.

Ordered completion uses a batch marker with a sentinel meaning idle; a fresh batch captures identifier and length from the ring, stays active across intervening obtains, and clears when the expected head arrives, otherwise length comes from stored inbound totals.

An RTC message moves from initialization to queued to notified to waited to validated to released; enqueue failure releases immediately since no completion will arrive, and reference counting frees request, response and envelope only on last drop.
Packed obtain, poll, availability, detach, enable, disable, reset and resize handlers plug into the generic queue operations vector, with ordered flavours substituting only obtain and availability.
The RTC class read hook rejects stopped or missing class instances, reads nanoseconds for its clock identifier, converts to whole seconds, then expands to calendar form.

Mapping failure during ordered insertion restores prior avail flags and counters, marks non head descriptors of the partial chain as unpublished with prior lap polarity so shorter reuse cannot leak availability, releases mapping extras, and reports an input output error.
Reclaiming unused buffers scans the whole ring for live heads and asserts that free count equals ring size afterwards, signalling internal accounting corruption otherwise.

Request transfer can fail with enqueue error, timeout, interruption, undersized header, device reported status, or length mismatch where actual response size differs from capacity, each propagated to the caller.

Device RTC statuses map to host errors with success meaning no error, operation not supported, invalid argument and no device preserved, and any other value including generic input output treated as input output error.

The packed wire uses VRING_PACKED_DESC_F_AVAIL together with VRING_PACKED_DESC_F_USED for completion, VRING_PACKED_EVENT_F_WRAP_CTR for generation selection, VRING_PACKED_EVENT_FLAG_DISABLE together with VRING_PACKED_EVENT_FLAG_ENABLE together with VRING_PACKED_EVENT_FLAG_DESC for suppression modes, and VIRTIO_F_RING_PACKED to select packed layout.

The RTC wire uses VIRTIO_RTC_REQ_READ to request time for a clock identifier, a header plus status envelope framed by VIRTIO_RTC_S_OK with VIRTIO_RTC_S_EOPNOTSUPP with VIRTIO_RTC_S_EINVAL with VIRTIO_RTC_S_ENODEV with VIRTIO_RTC_S_EIO, VIRTIO_RTC_COUNTER_ARM_VCT with CSID_ARM_ARCH_COUNTER for the ARM time source, and NSEC_PER_SEC to convert nanoseconds to seconds.
Reset clears both event cells and all descriptor flags to zero before reinitializing queue bookkeeping and packed event handling, establishing a known lap polarity.

Resize allocates a fresh ring plus state for the requested size, frees the old ring, attaches the new one and reinitializes, falling back to reset state and reporting memory exhaustion if allocation fails.
Class access serializes on an external guard: lookup from device private data fails when no class is attached, and stopped instances report busy without issuing device traffic.
